mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises real interest rates, reducing present value of future corporate cash flows and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which pressures firms to raise wages and prices, ultimately compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and rate hike regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) simultaneously falls below 3.5% signals an overheating labor market, which precedes a correction and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction and home-related equities and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive momentum in real personal savings (RSAFS) combined with a simultaneous decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over three months signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a consumer demand slowdown and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
